title: Reserved Capacity Surface Redesign: Simplified Contracts, Isolation Modes, and Burst UX
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines a redesign of the Reserved Capacity product surface to simplify contract concepts, introduce explicit "isolation modes" for tenants, and make burst behavior visible and controllable in the Console. Goals: reduce onboarding time for reserved pools, lower operator confusion about fallback behavior, and provide clearer runtime controls to balance latency SLOs and cost.
background: Current reserved capacity UX mixes terms (reservations, headroom, soft-evict, credits) across billing and runtime pages. Customers repeatedly ask: "How will my reserved commit behave during spikes?" and "Am I being preempted or throttled?" Engineering sees frequent support tickets where autoscale windows and fallback policies are misconfigured. We will consolidate concepts into a small set of primitives: Commitment, Isolation Mode, Burst Credits, and Autoscale Profile.
goals: Introduce three isolation modes: strict, buffered, and opportunistic (described below)
Expose burst credits ledger and projected depletion timeline in Console
Provide a single Reservation API that expresses commit size, min-alloc floor, autoscale profile, and isolation mode
Default UX that lets typical customers pick a preset (Standard, Business, Regulated) and advanced users tune policies
non_goals: Building a new billing engine (we will reuse existing billing events)
Adding cross-region failover automation for reserved pools (out of scope for this PRD)
Substituting or deprecating Dedicated policy primitives that are needed by existing enterprise contracts until migration plan is complete
scope: API: new /reservations v2 create/update/get that includes isolation_mode, burst_credit_policy, and autoscale_profile
Console: Reservation detail page redesign with ledger, timeline, and action buttons (add credits, change isolation, schedule prewarm)
Runtime: admit isolation mode flags into scheduler decision path (requires runtime gating behind feature flag)
Migration: bulk-migration tooling to map legacy reservations to v2 semantics with a preview step
out_of_scope: Automated billing adjustments for credit top-ups
Per-request cost-reduction suggestions (Optimize product handles token-level recommendations)
Dedicated autoscaler rewrite — we will add policy knobs that map to existing scaler behavior
user_stories: As an SRE for a SaaS product, I want to set a reservation to "buffered" so that my critical endpoints keep priority but noncritical workloads can be preempted
As a platform admin, I want a clear projected depletion timeline of burst credits so I can decide to top-up or schedule prewarm
As a compliance officer, I want a "strict" isolation preset that prevents spillback to multi-tenant capacity
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /reservations v2 accepts isolation_mode=(strict|buffered|opportunistic) and persists the value; GET returns consistent semantics
Console: Reservation detail page shows burst credit ledger, last 90 days usage sparkline, and an estimated depletion date when credits are being consumed
Runtime: When isolation_mode=strict, scheduler will refuse to route opportunistic fallback traffic to reserved capacity (integration test demonstrating refusal under synthetic contention)
Autoscale: autoscale_profile presets (conservative, default, aggressive) apply and result in measurable headroom behavior during load tests
Migration: migration tool produces a non-destructive preview report mapping 95% of legacy reservations to a recommended preset; manual review required for the remaining 5%
Telemetry: dashboards surface reservation_remaining_credits and alert if projected depletion within 48 hours with current usage pattern
Docs: Confluence PRD, Console help text, and API reference published prior to beta rollout
api_contracts: POST /v2/reservations {commit_gpus:int, min_alloc:float, isolation_mode:string, burst_credits:int, autoscale_profile:string, billing_state:optional} -> 201 reservation_id
GET /v2/reservations/{id} -> returns fields above and computed projected_depletion_iso8601
PATCH /v2/reservations/{id} -> allows bumping burst_credits and switching isolation_mode with optional immediate_preempt boolean
console_changes: New Reservations landing with list and filter by isolation_mode and depletion risk
Reservation detail redesign: ledger (top-ups, consumption events), projected timeline, quick actions (add credits, switch preset, schedule prewarm), migration badge if reservation is legacy
Preset selector with human-readable trade-offs and one-click migration helper for legacy reservations
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit metric reservation_remaining_credits (gauge) per reservation id
reservation_fallback_count (counter) when a request falls back off-reservation
reservation_preemption_events (counter) when a reserved request is preempted by higher priority tenant rule
Alert rule: reservation_remaining_credits < min(threshold, projected_consumption_48h) -> page oncall and send admin email
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta, internal customers) — API v2 available behind feature flag; Console beta for selected accounts; runtime gating enabled for low-traffic zones
Phase 2 (public opt-in) — default Console shows v2 but legacy remains available; migration tool shown with preview; telemetry dashboards public
Phase 3 (auto-migrate + deprecate legacy) — controlled migration for small accounts with consent + bulk operator migration windows; legacy API deprecated after 90 days
migration_strategy: Read-only preview mapping for all existing reservations with suggested preset and delta report
Customer-visible migration checklist and recommended action per reservation (auto-accept for trivial mappings)
Operator bulk-migration job with rollback; preflight dry-run and post-migration validation checks
dependencies: Runtime: scheduler change to evaluate isolation_mode flag (ENG-42111)
Billing: ensure top-up events map to billing ledger and invoicing (FIN-1182)
Console: new UI components and charting library upgrade (DES-3302)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers mis-configure isolation_mode and experience outages -> Mitigation: strong presets and default to buffered; explicit confirmation for strict changes
Risk: Unexpected billing items from top-ups -> Mitigation: billing team reviews top-up webhook and publishes pricing FAQ prior to beta
Risk: Scheduler regression under load -> Mitigation: runtime gating and stepwise rollout with load-testing in staging
open_questions: Should we allow negative burst credits as an overdraft? (engineering leans no)
How granular should projected_depletion be when a tenant has heterogeneous models with different token rates?
Do enterprise contracts require custom isolation_mode for specific routes rather than the whole reservation?
decisions: Adopt three isolation modes (strict, buffered, opportunistic) as canonical primitives
Expose burst credits in Console and allow manual top-ups; do not implement autopay for initial release
Map legacy headroom to buffered by default in migration preview
security_and_compliance: Feature flagged for VPC/private deployments until KMS audit is completed
Audit logs for reservation edits will contain actor, timestamp, and before/after snapshot (log schema to be agreed with Security)
qa_plan: Unit tests for API validation and enum acceptance for isolation_mode
Integration tests: synthetic contention verifying strict mode refusal, buffered mode partial fallback, opportunistic allowed fallback
End-to-end: Console action flows for top-up and isolation change using staging account with simulated billing webhook
